scene.label: Act 2, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Padua. A room in Baptista's house.
scene.location: Padua. A room in Baptista's house.

lines.text: Good sister, wrong me not, nor wrong yourself,
lines.plainText: Good sister wrong me not nor wrong yourself

lines.text: To make a bondmaid and a slave of me;
lines.plainText: To make a bondmaid and a slave of me

lines.text: That I disdain; but for these other gawds,
lines.plainText: That I disdain but for these other gawds

lines.text: Unbind my hands, I'll pull them off myself,
lines.plainText: Unbind my hands I'll pull them off myself

lines.text: Yea, all my raiment, to my petticoat;
lines.plainText: Yea all my raiment to my petticoat

lines.text: Or what you will command me will I do,
lines.plainText: Or what you will command me will I do

lines.text: So well I know my duty to my elders.
lines.plainText: So well I know my duty to my elders

lines.text: Of all thy suitors here I charge thee tell
lines.plainText: Of all thy suitors here I charge thee tell

lines.text: Whom thou lov'st best: see thou dissemble not.
lines.plainText: Whom thou lov'st best see thou dissemble not

lines.text: Believe me, sister, of all the men alive
lines.plainText: Believe me sister of all the men alive

lines.text: I never yet beheld that special face
lines.plainText: I never yet beheld that special face

lines.text: Which I could fancy more than any other.
lines.plainText: Which I could fancy more than any other

lines.text: Minion, thou liest. Is't not Hortensio?
lines.plainText: Minion thou liest Is't not Hortensio

lines.text: If you affect him, sister, here I swear
lines.plainText: If you affect him sister here I swear

lines.text: I'll plead for you myself but you shall have him.
lines.plainText: I'll plead for you myself but you shall have him

lines.text: O! then, belike, you fancy riches more:
lines.plainText: O then belike you fancy riches more

lines.text: You will have Gremio to keep you fair.
lines.plainText: You will have Gremio to keep you fair

lines.text: Is it for him you do envy me so?
lines.plainText: Is it for him you do envy me so

lines.text: Nay, then you jest; and now I well perceive
lines.plainText: Nay then you jest and now I well perceive

lines.text: You have but jested with me all this while:
lines.plainText: You have but jested with me all this while

lines.text: I prithee, sister Kate, untie my hands.
lines.plainText: I prithee sister Kate untie my hands

lines.text: If that be jest, then all the rest was so.
lines.plainText: If that be jest then all the rest was so

lines.text: Why, how now, dame! Whence grows this insolence?
lines.plainText: Why how now dame Whence grows this insolence

lines.text: Bianca, stand aside. Poor girl! she weeps.
lines.plainText: Bianca stand aside Poor girl she weeps

lines.text: Go ply thy needle; meddle not with her.
lines.plainText: Go ply thy needle meddle not with her

lines.text: For shame, thou hilding of a devilish spirit,
lines.plainText: For shame thou hilding of a devilish spirit

lines.text: Why dost thou wrong her that did ne'er wrong thee?
lines.plainText: Why dost thou wrong her that did ne'er wrong thee

lines.text: When did she cross thee with a bitter word?
lines.plainText: When did she cross thee with a bitter word

lines.text: Her silence flouts me, and I'll be reveng'd.
lines.plainText: Her silence flouts me and I'll be reveng'd

lines.text: What! in my sight? Bianca, get thee in.
lines.plainText: What in my sight Bianca get thee in

lines.text: What! will you not suffer me? Nay, now I see
lines.plainText: What will you not suffer me Nay now I see

lines.text: She is your treasure, she must have a husband;
lines.plainText: She is your treasure she must have a husband

lines.text: I must dance bare-foot on her wedding-day,
lines.plainText: I must dance barefoot on her weddingday

lines.text: And, for your love to her, lead apes in hell.
lines.plainText: And for your love to her lead apes in hell

lines.text: Talk not to me: I will go sit and weep
lines.plainText: Talk not to me I will go sit and weep

lines.text: Till I can find occasion of revenge.
lines.plainText: Till I can find occasion of revenge

lines.text: Was ever gentleman thus griev'd as I?
lines.plainText: Was ever gentleman thus griev'd as I

lines.text: But who comes here?
lines.plainText: But who comes here

content.text: Enter Gremio, with Lucentio in the habit of a mean man; Petruchio, with Hortensio as a musician; and Tranio, with Biondello bearing a lute and books.

lines.text: Good morrow, neighbour Baptista.
lines.plainText: Good morrow neighbour Baptista

lines.text: Good morrow, neighbour Gremio. God save you, gentlemen!
lines.plainText: Good morrow neighbour Gremio God save you gentlemen

lines.text: And you, good sir! Pray, have you not a daughter
lines.plainText: And you good sir Pray have you not a daughter

lines.text: Call'd Katherina, fair and virtuous?
lines.plainText: Call'd Katherina fair and virtuous

lines.text: I have a daughter, sir, call'd Katherina.
lines.plainText: I have a daughter sir call'd Katherina

lines.text: You are too blunt: go to it orderly.
lines.plainText: You are too blunt go to it orderly

lines.text: You wrong me, Signior Gremio: give me leave.
lines.plainText: You wrong me Signior Gremio give me leave

lines.text: I am a gentleman of Verona, sir,
lines.plainText: I am a gentleman of Verona sir

lines.text: That, hearing of her beauty and her wit,
lines.plainText: That hearing of her beauty and her wit

lines.text: Her affability and bashful modesty,
lines.plainText: Her affability and bashful modesty

lines.text: Her wondrous qualities and mild behaviour,
lines.plainText: Her wondrous qualities and mild behaviour

lines.text: Am bold to show myself a forward guest
lines.plainText: Am bold to show myself a forward guest

lines.text: Within your house, to make mine eye the witness
lines.plainText: Within your house to make mine eye the witness

lines.text: Of that report which I so oft have heard.
lines.plainText: Of that report which I so oft have heard

lines.text: And, for an entrance to my entertainment,
lines.plainText: And for an entrance to my entertainment

lines.text: I do present you with a man of mine,
lines.plainText: I do present you with a man of mine

lines.text: Y'are welcome, sir, and he for your good sake;
lines.plainText: Y'are welcome sir and he for your good sake

lines.text: But for my daughter Katherine, this I know,
lines.plainText: But for my daughter Katherine this I know

lines.text: She is not for your turn, the more my grief.
lines.plainText: She is not for your turn the more my grief

lines.text: I see you do not mean to part with her;
lines.plainText: I see you do not mean to part with her

lines.text: Or else you like not of my company.
lines.plainText: Or else you like not of my company

lines.text: Mistake me not; I speak but as I find.
lines.plainText: Mistake me not I speak but as I find

lines.text: Whence are you, sir? What may I call your name?
lines.plainText: Whence are you sir What may I call your name

lines.text: Petruchio is my name, Antonio's son;
lines.plainText: Petruchio is my name Antonio's son

lines.text: A man well known throughout all Italy.
lines.plainText: A man well known throughout all Italy

lines.text: I know him well: you are welcome for his sake.
lines.plainText: I know him well you are welcome for his sake

lines.text: Saving your tale, Petruchio, I pray,
lines.plainText: Saving your tale Petruchio I pray

lines.text: Let us, that are poor petitioners, speak too.
lines.plainText: Let us that are poor petitioners speak too

lines.text: Backare! you are marvellous forward.
lines.plainText: Backare you are marvellous forward

lines.text: O, pardon me, Signior Gremio; I would fain be doing.
lines.plainText: O pardon me Signior Gremio I would fain be doing

lines.text: I doubt it not, sir; but you will curse your wooing. Neighbour, this is a gift very grateful, I am sure of it. To express the like kindness, myself, that have been more kindly beholding to you than any, freely give unto you this young scholar,
lines.plainText: I doubt it not sir but you will curse your wooing Neighbour this is a gift very grateful I am sure of it To express the like kindness myself that have been more kindly beholding to you than any freely give unto you this young scholar

lines.text: A thousand thanks, Signior Gremio; welcome, good Cambio. [To Tranio.] But, gentle sir, methinks you walk like a stranger. May I be so bold to know the cause of your coming?
lines.plainText: A thousand thanks Signior Gremio welcome good Cambio To Tranio But gentle sir methinks you walk like a stranger May I be so bold to know the cause of your coming

lines.text: Pardon me, sir, the boldness is mine own,
lines.plainText: Pardon me sir the boldness is mine own

lines.text: That, being a stranger in this city here,
lines.plainText: That being a stranger in this city here

lines.text: Do make myself a suitor to your daughter,
lines.plainText: Do make myself a suitor to your daughter

lines.text: Unto Bianca, fair and virtuous.
lines.plainText: Unto Bianca fair and virtuous

lines.text: Nor is your firm resolve unknown to me,
lines.plainText: Nor is your firm resolve unknown to me

lines.text: In the preferment of the eldest sister.
lines.plainText: In the preferment of the eldest sister

lines.text: This liberty is all that I request,
lines.plainText: This liberty is all that I request

lines.text: That, upon knowledge of my parentage,
lines.plainText: That upon knowledge of my parentage

lines.text: I may have welcome 'mongst the rest that woo,
lines.plainText: I may have welcome 'mongst the rest that woo

lines.text: And free access and favour as the rest:
lines.plainText: And free access and favour as the rest

lines.text: And, toward the education of your daughters,
lines.plainText: And toward the education of your daughters

lines.text: I here bestow a simple instrument,
lines.plainText: I here bestow a simple instrument

lines.text: And this small packet of Greek and Latin books:
lines.plainText: And this small packet of Greek and Latin books

lines.text: If you accept them, then their worth is great.
lines.plainText: If you accept them then their worth is great

lines.text: Lucentio is your name, of whence, I pray?
lines.plainText: Lucentio is your name of whence I pray

lines.text: Of Pisa, sir; son to Vincentio.
lines.plainText: Of Pisa sir son to Vincentio

lines.text: A mighty man of Pisa: by report
lines.plainText: A mighty man of Pisa by report

lines.text: I know him well: you are very welcome, sir.
lines.plainText: I know him well you are very welcome sir

lines.text: [To Hortensio.] Take you the lute,
lines.plainText: To Hortensio Take you the lute

lines.text: [To Lucentio.] and you the set of books;
lines.plainText: To Lucentio and you the set of books

lines.text: You shall go see your pupils presently.
lines.plainText: You shall go see your pupils presently

lines.text: Holla, within!
lines.plainText: Holla within

lines.text: Signior Baptista, my business asketh haste,
lines.plainText: Signior Baptista my business asketh haste

lines.text: And every day I cannot come to woo.
lines.plainText: And every day I cannot come to woo

lines.text: You knew my father well, and in him me,
lines.plainText: You knew my father well and in him me

lines.text: Left solely heir to all his lands and goods,
lines.plainText: Left solely heir to all his lands and goods

lines.text: Which I have bettered rather than decreas'd:
lines.plainText: Which I have bettered rather than decreas'd

lines.text: Then tell me, if I get your daughter's love,
lines.plainText: Then tell me if I get your daughter's love

lines.text: What dowry shall I have with her to wife?
lines.plainText: What dowry shall I have with her to wife

lines.text: After my death, the one half of my lands,
lines.plainText: After my death the one half of my lands

lines.text: And in possession twenty thousand crowns.
lines.plainText: And in possession twenty thousand crowns

lines.text: And, for that dowry, I'll assure her of
lines.plainText: And for that dowry I'll assure her of

lines.text: Her widowhood, be it that she survive me,
lines.plainText: Her widowhood be it that she survive me

lines.text: In all my lands and leases whatsoever.
lines.plainText: In all my lands and leases whatsoever

lines.text: Let specialities be therefore drawn between us,
lines.plainText: Let specialities be therefore drawn between us

lines.text: That covenants may be kept on either hand.
lines.plainText: That covenants may be kept on either hand

lines.text: Ay, when the special thing is well obtain'd,
lines.plainText: Ay when the special thing is well obtain'd

lines.text: That is, her love; for that is all in all.
lines.plainText: That is her love for that is all in all

lines.text: Why, that is nothing; for I tell you, father,
lines.plainText: Why that is nothing for I tell you father

lines.text: I am as peremptory as she proud-minded;
lines.plainText: I am as peremptory as she proudminded

lines.text: And where two raging fires meet together,
lines.plainText: And where two raging fires meet together

lines.text: They do consume the thing that feeds their fury:
lines.plainText: They do consume the thing that feeds their fury

lines.text: Though little fire grows great with little wind,
lines.plainText: Though little fire grows great with little wind

lines.text: Yet extreme gusts will blow out fire and all;
lines.plainText: Yet extreme gusts will blow out fire and all

lines.plainText: So I to her and so she yields to me

lines.text: For I am rough and woo not like a babe.
lines.plainText: For I am rough and woo not like a babe

lines.text: Well mayst thou woo, and happy be thy speed!
lines.plainText: Well mayst thou woo and happy be thy speed

lines.text: But be thou arm'd for some unhappy words.
lines.plainText: But be thou arm'd for some unhappy words

lines.text: Ay, to the proof, as mountains are for winds,
lines.plainText: Ay to the proof as mountains are for winds

lines.text: That shake not though they blow perpetually.
lines.plainText: That shake not though they blow perpetually

content.text: Re-enter Hortensio, with his head broke.

lines.text: How now, my friend! Why dost thou look so pale?
lines.plainText: How now my friend Why dost thou look so pale

lines.text: For fear, I promise you, if I look pale.
lines.plainText: For fear I promise you if I look pale

lines.text: What, will my daughter prove a good musician?
lines.plainText: What will my daughter prove a good musician

lines.text: I think she'll sooner prove a soldier:
lines.plainText: I think she'll sooner prove a soldier

lines.plainText: Iron may hold with her but never lutes

lines.plainText: Why then thou canst not break her to the lute

lines.plainText: Why no for she hath broke the lute to me

lines.plainText: I did but tell her she mistook her frets

lines.plainText: And bow'd her hand to teach her fingering

lines.plainText: When with a most impatient devilish spirit

lines.plainText: 'Frets call you these' quoth she 'I'll fume with them'

lines.plainText: And with that word she struck me on the head

lines.plainText: And through the instrument my pate made way

lines.plainText: And there I stood amazed for a while

lines.plainText: As on a pillory looking through the lute

lines.plainText: While she did call me rascal fiddler

lines.plainText: And twangling Jack with twenty such vile terms

lines.plainText: As had she studied to misuse me so

lines.text: Now, by the world, it is a lusty wench!
lines.plainText: Now by the world it is a lusty wench

lines.plainText: I love her ten times more than e'er I did

lines.plainText: O how I long to have some chat with her

lines.text: She's apt to learn, and thankful for good turns.

lines.plainText: Or shall I send my daughter Kate to you

lines.text: I pray you do.
lines.plainText: I pray you do

lines.plainText: Well have you heard but something hard of hearing

lines.plainText: They call me Katherine that do talk of me

lines.plainText: You lie in faith for you are call'd plain Kate

lines.text: And bonny Kate, and sometimes Kate the curst;
lines.plainText: And bonny Kate and sometimes Kate the curst

lines.text: But, Kate, the prettiest Kate in Christendom,
lines.plainText: But Kate the prettiest Kate in Christendom

lines.text: Kate of Kate Hall, my super-dainty Kate,
lines.plainText: Kate of Kate Hall my superdainty Kate

lines.text: For dainties are all Kates, and therefore, Kate,
lines.plainText: For dainties are all Kates and therefore Kate

lines.plainText: Take this of me Kate of my consolation

lines.text: Hearing thy mildness prais'd in every town,
lines.plainText: Hearing thy mildness prais'd in every town

lines.text: Thy virtues spoke of, and thy beauty sounded,—
lines.plainText: Thy virtues spoke of and thy beauty sounded

lines.plainText: Yet not so deeply as to thee belongs

lines.plainText: Myself am mov'd to woo thee for my wife

lines.plainText: Women are made to bear and so are you

lines.plainText: No such jade as bear you if me you mean

lines.plainText: Too light for such a swain as you to catch

lines.plainText: Ay for a turtle as he takes a buzzard

lines.text: That I'll try.
lines.plainText: That I'll try

lines.plainText: I swear I'll cuff you if you strike again

lines.plainText: It is my fashion when I see a crab

lines.plainText: Why here's no crab and therefore look not sour

lines.plainText: Thus in plain terms your father hath consented

lines.plainText: That you shall be my wife your dowry 'greed on

lines.text: And will you, nill you, I will marry you.
lines.plainText: And will you nill you I will marry you

lines.text: Now, Kate, I am a husband for your turn;
lines.plainText: Now Kate I am a husband for your turn

lines.text: For, by this light, whereby I see thy beauty,—
lines.plainText: For by this light whereby I see thy beauty

lines.text: Thy beauty that doth make me like thee well,—
lines.plainText: Thy beauty that doth make me like thee well

lines.text: Thou must be married to no man but me;
lines.plainText: Thou must be married to no man but me

lines.text: For I am he am born to tame you, Kate,
lines.plainText: For I am he am born to tame you Kate

lines.text: And bring you from a wild Kate to a Kate
lines.plainText: And bring you from a wild Kate to a Kate

lines.text: Conformable as other household Kates.

lines.plainText: Now Signior Petruchio how speed you with my daughter

lines.text: How but well, sir? how but well?

lines.text: It were impossible I should speed amiss.
lines.plainText: It were impossible I should speed amiss

lines.plainText: Why how now daughter Katherine in your dumps

lines.plainText: You have show'd a tender fatherly regard

lines.text: To wish me wed to one half lunatic,
lines.plainText: To wish me wed to one half lunatic

lines.plainText: If she and I be pleas'd what's that to you

lines.plainText: She hung about my neck and kiss on kiss

lines.plainText: That in a twink she won me to her love

lines.plainText: A meacock wretch can make the curstest shrew

lines.plainText: To buy apparel 'gainst the weddingday

lines.plainText: I will be sure my Katherine shall be fine

lines.plainText: I know not what to say but give me your hands

lines.plainText: Was ever match clapp'd up so suddenly

lines.plainText: Faith gentlemen now I play a merchant's part

lines.text: And venture madly on a desperate mart.
lines.plainText: And venture madly on a desperate mart

lines.plainText: The gain I seek is quiet in the match

lines.plainText: No doubt but he hath got a quiet catch

lines.text: My hangings all of Tyrian tapestry;

lines.text: In cypress chests my arras counterpoints,

lines.text: Costly apparel, tents, and canopies,

lines.text: Fine linen, Turkey cushions boss'd with pearl,
lines.plainText: Fine linen Turkey cushions boss'd with pearl

lines.text: Valance of Venice gold in needlework;
lines.plainText: Valance of Venice gold in needlework

lines.text: Pewter and brass, and all things that belong
lines.plainText: Pewter and brass and all things that belong

lines.plainText: To house or housekeeping then at my farm

lines.text: I have a hundred milch-kine to the pail,
lines.plainText: I have a hundred milchkine to the pail

lines.plainText: Six score fat oxen standing in my stalls

lines.plainText: And all things answerable to this portion

lines.plainText: Myself am struck in years I must confess

lines.plainText: And if I die tomorrow this is hers

lines.plainText: If whilst I live she will be only mine

lines.plainText: I am my father's heir and only son

lines.plainText: I'll leave her houses three or four as good

lines.plainText: Within rich Pisa's walls as anyone

lines.plainText: That she shall have besides an argosy
